# Operator Paths Reference

The six guided paths on the agent operating surface: what each one is for, what it accepts, what it returns, which CLI commands it composes, and where its write boundary sits.

## Overview

An operator path is a **guided composition of CLI commands that already exist**. No path adds a `glassfrog` subcommand, an API capability, a flag, or an argument. Each is a pair of plugin artifacts:

| Artifact | Role |
|---|---|
| `plugin/skills/<path>/SKILL.md` | Loaded on demand when the caller's need matches its `description`. States when to reach for the path and the workflow, then delegates. |
| `plugin/agents/<agent>.md` | The subagent that executes the work in its own context and returns a synthesized result. Raw command output never leaves that context. |

Input is natural language — a concern, an action, a tension, an id. There are no flags on either artifact.

All six paths ride on [operator orientation](../explanation/the-agent-operating-surface.md), which owns output-format, pagination, and exit-code mechanics. The paths defer to it rather than restating those. For per-command flags they defer to `glassfrog <command> --help`.

### The Six Paths

| Path | Skill name | Agent | Writes | Takes | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Governance Navigation | `governance-navigation` | `governance-navigator` | none | a free-form concern | synthesized picture |
| Constraint Discovery | `constraint-discovery` | `constraint-navigator` | none | a wanted action | synthesized picture + characterization |
| Tension Processing | `tension-processing` | `tension-processor` | tension writes (ungated) | a voiced tension + sensing role | tension record |
| Proposal Drafting | `proposal-drafting` | `proposal-drafter` | one gated create, in-subagent | an anchor `ten_` id + intended change | draft record |
| Proposal Circulation | `proposal-circulation` | `proposal-circulator` | two gated transitions, in-subagent | a `prp_` id + intent | circulation record |
| Proposal Impact Review | `proposal-impact-review` | `proposal-impact-reviewer` | one gated respond, **in caller context** | a `prp_` id, or "what's pending on me?" | impact picture, then recorded response |

Every agent carries the same tool grant — `Bash, Read, Grep, Glob` — and `model: inherit`. `Write` and `Edit` are withheld from all six.

### Handoff Chain

The paths compose into a chain. Each handoff is an id, and each path stops at its boundary rather than continuing into the next.

```
concern ──► Governance Navigation ──► the governance around it
action  ──► Constraint Discovery  ──► what governs it
tension ──► Tension Processing ──ten_──► Proposal Drafting ──prp_──► Proposal Circulation
                                                                └──► (withdraw) ──prp_──► Proposal Drafting
circulating proposal ──► Proposal Impact Review ──► recorded response
```

---

## Governance Navigation Path

Takes a practitioner's free-form concern — usually a tension, sensed but not yet located in the structure — and returns a synthesized picture of the governance around it.

### Composed Commands

Read-only. Seven top-level read leaves:

`search`, `roles`, `tree`, `fillers`, `subrole-actors`, `domains`, `policies`

### Traversal

`search` on the concern → resolve matched role ids via `roles [id]` → `fillers` / `subrole-actors` for who fills them → `domains` / `policies` for the governing governance, following into sub-roles only as far as relevance warrants. Multi-page results are paged through in full before the picture is narrowed.

### Output Shape

| Element | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `roles` | `Role[]` | Each: `id` (always `role_…` — a circle is a role with `type: circle`; there is no `circle_` id namespace), `name`, a one-line relevance to the concern |
| `fillers` | per-role list | Each role's actors: `actor_id` (`per_` / `agt_`), `name` |
| `domains` | `Domain[]` | Governing domains in view: `id`, `role_id`, brief |
| `policies` | `Policy[]` | Governing policies in view: `id`, `role_id`, brief |
| `notes` | `string[]` | Narrowing / failure notes |

Every element carries the id needed to read it again. This is a contract shape, not a serialization format — the agent presents it as readable prose, and each id remains actionable.

### Boundary

Never rules on permission. An authority question is answered by surfacing the governing domains and policies and deferring the verdict to Constraint Discovery.

---

## Constraint Discovery Path

The mirror of Governance Navigation. Takes an action a practitioner wants to take and returns what governs it, so the operator learns whether it is theirs to do.

### Composed Commands

Read-only. Seven read leaves:

`search`, `roles`, `tree`, `domains`, `policies`, `policy`, `me roles`

`domains` and `policies` are top-level commands, not `roles` subcommands. `me roles` is the `roles` subcommand of `me`.

### Clarify-When-Vague

If the action is too vague to search for its governing governance, the **skill** asks the operator to sharpen it — in the caller's context, before the agent is ever invoked. If the operator declines, the path stops. No action is fabricated. The agent has no clarify branch.

### Traversal

`search` on the action → resolve matched ids into `roles [id]` / `domains <role_id>` / `policies <role_id>` (or `policy <pol_id>` when search returns a policy directly) → `me roles` to mark ownership → follow into sub-roles via `tree` only as far as relevance warrants.

### Output Shape

| Element | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | `string` | The well-formed action the picture is about, echoed for confirmation |
| `domains` | `Domain[]` | `id`, `role_id`, `role_name`, brief, and `owned_by_caller` |
| `policies` | `Policy[]` | `id` (`pol_…`), `role_id`, brief of what it grants or limits |
| `characterization` | `string` | A composed summary of the authority situation, drawn from the record |
| `notes` | `string[]` | Narrowing / failure / uncertainty notes |

#### `owned_by_caller` is tri-state

`true` / `false` / **uncertain** — whether `role_id` is among the caller's own roles. It is **uncertain** when the `me roles` list is incomplete, because `me roles` does not follow pagination. An unconfirmed match is never reported as a definite `false`, so a possibly-missing own-role is never misattributed as another role's.

#### `characterization` is composed, not an enum

It is assembled from three independent parts, not a single mutually-exclusive value:

1. **The domain finding** — the governing domain is held by a role the caller fills (within their own authority), held by another role (named, with its id, so it needs that role's permission or a proposal), or no domain in the record governs it (the absence is reported plainly — **not** as a "you are permitted" verdict).
2. **Any policies** that shape or limit the action, surfaced **even when the action is within the caller's own domain**. Policies compose with the domain finding; they are never an alternative to it.
3. **Whether the action is a change to governance structure** — which goes through a proposal by default.

When the match is ambiguous, the characterization is *the record does not clearly answer*, with what was found. It is never an allow/deny verdict computed from local rules.

### Boundary

Surfaces what the record says. Never computes a permission verdict, never reimplements permission rules locally.

## Tension Processing Path

Takes a voiced tension and the role that senses it, and works it into a well-formed tension record.

### Composed Commands

Six `tension` leaves — three situating reads and three operational writes:

| Leaf | Kind |
|---|---|
| `tension list` | read |
| `tension get` | read |
| `tension subroles` | read |
| `tension create` | write (ungated by design) |
| `tension update` | write (ungated by design) |
| `tension discard` | write (ungated by design) |

No `proposal` leaf ever appears here.

### Workflow

`tension list <role-id>` + `tension subroles <role-id>` to situate against what is already sensed → `tension create <role-id>` if the tension is new → `tension update <ten-id>` to refine, or `tension discard <ten-id>` to retire, as the practitioner directs. Situating lists are paged through in full before judging duplicates.

### Output Shape

| Element | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tension` | `Tension` | `id` (`ten_…`), `sensing_role_id` (`role_…`), `body`, `label?`, `status` |
| `situating` | `Tension[]` | The tensions already sensed on the role and rolled up from its sub-roles that the processor weighed |
| `action` | `string` | `captured` \| `refined` \| `retired` \| `surfaced-existing` \| `none` |
| `handoff` | `string?` | The `ten_` id to feed Proposal Drafting, when the tension is ready to become a governance change. Absent when not ready |
| `notes` | `string[]` | Duplicate / failure / decision notes |

### Boundary

Stops at the moment the tension is ready to become a governance change — it sets `handoff` and stops. It never drafts, creates, or circulates a proposal. Tension writes are ungated by design; the fence this path must not cross is a *proposal* write.

---

## Proposal Drafting Path

Takes a well-formed anchor tension that is ready to become a governance change, and creates the draft proposal.

### Composed Commands

Four leaves — three grounding/situating reads and one gated write:

| Leaf | Kind |
|---|---|
| `tension get` | read |
| `proposal list` | read |
| `proposal get` | read |
| `proposal create` | **gated write** |

### Workflow

`tension get <ten-id>` to ground the draft → `proposal list --role-id <circle> --status draft` (full walk) to situate, `proposal get <prp-id>` to inspect a candidate match → assemble the change set (a JSON array, non-empty `type` per element) → narrate the anchor and change set → run `proposal create <ten-id> --changes '<inline JSON>'`.

The write-safety hook then interposes: the practitioner sees the exact command, **payload inline**, and confirms or declines. Inline is deliberate — it is the only form that keeps the confirmation informative. If the change set is too unwieldy for an inline command line, the agent surfaces that to the caller rather than smuggling it through a hidden file.

### Output Shape

| Element | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `draft` | `Proposal?` | `id` (`prp_…`), `status` (`draft`), `tension_id` (`ten_…`), `changes` as accepted. Absent when nothing was created |
| `anchor` | `Tension` | The tension the draft is grounded in: `id`, `sensing_role_id`, one-line summary |
| `situating` | `Proposal[]` | The in-flight proposals weighed during the duplicate check |
| `action` | `string` | `created` \| `surfaced-existing` \| `declined` \| `none` |
| `handoff` | `string?` | The `prp_` id to feed Proposal Circulation, when a draft exists and is ready to circulate |
| `notes` | `string[]` | Duplicate / failure / decision notes |

### Boundary

Creates the draft and stops. Never advances, responds to, or withdraws a proposal. When a matching draft is already in flight it returns that one with `action: surfaced-existing` and creates nothing.

---

## Proposal Circulation Path

Takes a proposal that already exists and moves or watches it through the consent lifecycle.

### Composed Commands

Four leaves — two reads and two gated bodyless transitions:

| Leaf | Kind |
|---|---|
| `proposal get` | read |
| `proposal list` | read |
| `proposal propose` | **gated write** (advance) |
| `proposal withdraw` | **gated write** (pull back to draft) |

Each write is confirmed independently.

### Output Shape

| Element | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `proposal` | `Proposal?` | The target **exactly as the server last returned it**: `id`, `status`, `response_summary`, `response_deadline`, `available_transitions`. After an advance: `proposed_outside_meeting` with the server-set deadline and the implicit `no_objection` in the summary. After a withdraw: back in `draft` with `proposed_at` / `response_deadline` cleared. Absent only when the grounding read itself failed |
| `situating` | `Proposal[]?` | The circle's in-flight proposals when the picture was drawn. Absent when not relevant to the intent |
| `action` | `string` | `advanced` \| `monitored` \| `withdrawn` \| `declined` \| `none` |
| `handoff` | `string?` | After a withdraw: the `prp_` id to feed back to Proposal Drafting for re-editing |
| `notes` | `string[]` | Failure / decision notes |

No field is synthesized. **Acceptance is never computed client-side** — the parent proposal's status is the signal, exactly as returned. `available_transitions` is narration only: the transition is issued and the server's `422` surfaced plainly rather than pre-gated locally.

### Boundary

Never records a consent response — that is Proposal Impact Review. Never assembles changes or creates a draft — that is Proposal Drafting.

---

## Proposal Impact Review Path

The responder's counterpart to Proposal Circulation. Shows the operator what a circulating proposal would change for their own roles, actions, and projects, and then records their chosen consent response.

### Composed Commands

Ten leaves — nine reads the agent may run, plus one gated write reserved to the skill:

| Leaf | Kind | Run by |
|---|---|---|
| `proposal get` | read | agent |
| `proposal list` | read | agent |
| `me` | read | agent |
| `me roles` | read | agent |
| `me actions` | read | agent |
| `me projects` | read | agent |
| `roles` | read | agent |
| `domains` | read | agent |
| `policies` | read | agent |
| `proposal respond` | **gated write** | **the skill, in the caller's context** |

### The Write Runs Outside the Subagent

Unlike Proposal Drafting and Proposal Circulation, the gated write does **not** run inside the subagent. The operator's decision structurally splits the workflow at the read/write seam: an isolated subagent cannot ask the operator to decide, so the write runs in the caller's context, where the write-safety gate fires identically.

The agent that draws the picture **has no respond mode**. Its output shape has no verdict field, and its prompt forbids all four proposal writes — the strictest fence of the six. If a caller asks the agent to record the response, it refuses by name: recording the response is the skill's caller-context step, after the operator decides.

### Output Shape

| Element | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `proposal` | `Proposal?` | The target **exactly as the server returned it**: `id`, `status`, `response_summary`, `response_deadline`, `available_transitions`. Absent when the grounding read failed, or in pending-list mode |
| `changes` | `Change[]?` | The change set drawn out: each element's type (e.g. `CreateRole`, `UpdateAccountability`) and the governance it targets (role/domain/policy id and name where the record carries one). Reflected from the record, never re-interpreted into a ruling |
| `footprint` | `Footprint?` | The operator's current governance as read: identity (from `me`), roles filled, actions held, projects carried — each with its id. Absent only when every footprint read failed |
| `footprint_coverage` | `string` | **Tri-state**: `complete` \| `incomplete` (the `me roles` incompleteness signal fired) \| `unknown` (a footprint read failed). Never a silent `complete` |
| `intersections` | `Intersection[]` | Where the change set lands on the operator: per affected element — the change, the touched role/action/project, and the current-vs-proposed read-back. An empty array is the honest no-impact case, qualified per `footprint_coverage` |
| `pending` | `Proposal[]?` | Pending-list mode only: the circulating proposals awaiting the operator, each with `id`, `status`, `response_deadline`, one-line summary |
| `notes` | `string[]` | Failure / qualifier notes |

There is no verdict field. The picture contains **no recommended response and no objection ruling** — the operator judges.

### Reviews Inform, Never Decide

The decision value enters the flow only from the operator, in the caller's context, after the picture exists. "No objections found" in a picture is **not** an instruction to answer `no_objection`. The skill forbids inferring a value from the picture, and the output shape has no field to smuggle one through.

### Boundary

Never advances, monitors, or withdraws the operator's own proposal — that is Proposal Circulation. Never assembles changes or creates a draft — that is Proposal Drafting. Never rules on authority — that is Constraint Discovery.

---

## Write Gating

The write-safety guardrail gates governance writes at the operator layer. Membership is defined by a single registry file that every path's drift guard checks against.

| Command | Gated |
|---|---|
| `proposal create` | yes |
| `proposal propose` | yes |
| `proposal withdraw` | yes |
| `proposal respond` | yes |
| `tension create` / `update` / `discard` | no — ungated by design |
| every read leaf | no |

### The Tool Grant Is Not the Fence

Each agent's `tools` grant covers *Claude tools*, not individual `glassfrog` subcommands. Withholding `Write` and `Edit` blocks workspace mutation, but it cannot by itself stop a `glassfrog` write issued through `Bash`. The fence is therefore **layered**:

1. **The agent prompt** scopes execution to that path's registered leaves and names the writes it must not run.
2. **The write-safety hook** (`PreToolUse` on `Bash`) interposes the human confirmation on any registered gated leaf.

Hook coverage inside subagent calls was empirically confirmed during Tension Processing — the hook input carries an `agent_id`. A gated write that executes without a confirmation prompt is a defect.

## Composed-Leaf Registries and Drift Guards

Each path's composed leaves are written **once** in a committed registry file, consumed by both the agent artifact's command reference and a drift guard test under `internal/build`. One file, two (or three) consumers, no duplicated list.

| Path | Registry file | Leaves |
|---|---|---|
| Governance Navigation | `plugin/agents/composed-reads.txt` | 7 reads |
| Constraint Discovery | `plugin/agents/constraint-discovery-composed-reads.txt` | 7 reads |
| Tension Processing | `plugin/agents/tension-processing-commands.txt` | 3 reads + 3 ungated writes |
| Proposal Drafting | `plugin/agents/proposal-drafting-commands.txt` | 3 reads + 1 gated write |
| Proposal Circulation | `plugin/agents/proposal-circulation-commands.txt` | 2 reads + 2 gated writes |
| Proposal Impact Review | `plugin/agents/proposal-impact-review-commands.txt` | 9 reads + 1 gated write |

Each guard checks that every leaf still resolves in the shipped CLI **and** that the gate posture holds per leaf — a named write is a member of the gated registry, and the named reads are absent from it. Per-leaf assertions mean a read/write swap across the gate cannot satisfy the guard by count alone.

A red guard means a path's artifacts name a command the CLI no longer exposes, or a leaf moved across the gate. Fix the artifact, or fix the claim.

## Failure Behavior

All six paths share the same failure posture: surface what failed, return what succeeded, never fabricate.

| Condition | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Search or grounding read matches nothing | An explicit "nothing found — refine" note. No fabricated roles, governance, or ids |
| A read fails mid-traversal | The failure is named in `notes` and the result is built from the reads that succeeded. Never aborted, never invented |
| A partial paged walk | The gathered set is weighed and flagged incomplete |
| Over-broad input (many matches) | The full result set is paged through, then narrowed to the most relevant with a "narrowed — refine" note. Never a silent single-page cap |
| A write is rejected (`403`, `404`, `422`) | The failure is surfaced by name with `action: none`. No fabricated `ten_` / `prp_` / `prr_` id, no retry — a retry is itself a gated write needing fresh confirmation |
| Confirmation declined at the gate | `action: declined`, nothing written. An outcome, not an error |
| `me roles` signals incompleteness | Coverage marked `incomplete` / `uncertain`; every negative conclusion qualified. Never an unqualified negative |
| The skill file is missing or has no `description` | The path is not discoverable — callers fall back to driving the commands by hand |
| The agent file is missing or unregistered | The delegation target is absent; the skill's workflow is still readable as guidance, degraded |
| The agent's `tools` grant omits `Bash` | The agent cannot invoke `glassfrog` at all — a misconfiguration, not a safety win |

A `403` on a Premium async-proposal write renders through the possibility-framed [plan-limit signal](plan-limit-signal.md).

HTTP error shapes, status rendering, optimistic concurrency (`If-Match` / `412`), and rate-limit handling are not this layer's concern — they belong to the CLI the agents drive, and reach the operator through the exit-code reactions that operator orientation documents.
